scenario.description: An HR business partner must approve a returning employee's reintegration plan, including work hours, support, role boundaries, and safeguards for an existing coworker relationship.

shared_context.S1: Noor is scheduled to return to the operations team after a six-month leave.
shared_context.S2: Mara must approve the written reintegration plan before Noor resumes regular assignments.
shared_context.S3: The plan can set temporary hours, training support, role boundaries, and communication arrangements.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal return-to-work process, Mara holds a round-robin planning meeting with Noor, Elias, Maya, and Grant before approving the plan.
shared_context.S5: Mara uses the department's standard return-to-work worksheet to review the schedule, training, communication arrangements, and initial duties.
shared_context.S6: The return-to-work meeting is scheduled to conclude with Mara reviewing and approving the completed reintegration plan.

PF1.text: Noor can reliably work 24 hours per week for the first six weeks because of an ongoing family-care arrangement; Noor has discussed the arrangement only with a trusted coworker and has not yet raised the exact limit with Mara.

PF2.text: Elias observed that Noor needs three paired shadowing sessions on the updated case-management process before handling cases independently; Elias has not added this observation to the return paperwork.

PF3.text: Maya and Noor had a serious communication breakdown before Noor's leave, and Maya will not participate in direct one-to-one meetings with Noor during the first six weeks; Maya has not made this condition in a formal request.

PF4.text: Grant promised Noor before the leave that the initial return role would focus on internal process support rather than client escalation work; the promise was informal and is absent from the draft plan.

acceptance_conditions: Noor's first six weeks must be set at exactly 24 hours per week.
The plan must include exactly three paired shadowing sessions on the updated case-management process.
Direct one-to-one meetings between Noor and Maya must be prohibited during the first six weeks.
Noor's initial role must be limited to internal process support, with client escalation work disallowed during the initial six weeks.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

provenance_checks.P4: 'PF4' in credited_facts and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Noor's exact family-care limit changes the first-six-weeks schedule from an ordinary full-time return to exactly 24 hours per week.
Elias's observation changes the support plan to exactly three paired shadowing sessions on the updated case-management process.
Maya's specific boundary changes the communication arrangement from allowing ordinary one-to-ones to prohibiting direct one-to-one meetings for six weeks.
Grant's informal promise changes the initial role decision to internal process support and changes client escalation work from allowed to disallowed during the first six weeks.
